correctness.rationale: Removed caps are pairwise disjoint in interiors for 0<=t<=1/2; each is homothetic about a vertex with volume t^d and barycentric mean (1-t)e_i+t mu. By permutation symmetry retained centroid stays mu and covariance is a scalar on the tangent hyperplane. Subtracting exact Dirichlet simplex cap second moments gives normalized inertia J_t/J0=[1-BA]/[1-B], hence the isotropic-ratio formula with intrinsic reference volume. Differentiation yields a positive factor times S_d(t)=1-d+2(d+1)t-(d+3)t^2-2(d+1)t^d(1-t). The stated factorizations at d=2,3,4 and monotone upper bound P_d(t)<=P_d(1/2)=(5-d)/4 for d>=5 prove all monotonicity cases. Independently checked derivative identity at d=2..11 and endpoints using symbolic algebra; finite checks are not a proof for all d.

value.rationale: This gives an explicit affine-invariant shape functional along a geometrically natural whole truncation path, with a genuine dimension-2 phase reversal and dimension>=3 strict monotonicity. The exact high-dimensional rectification gap and sharp exceptional planar minimum are meaningful for extremal isotropic geometry; the proof is more than a known simplex constant substitution.

final_claim: For uniformly barycentrically truncated d-simplex K_(d,t), 0<=t<=1/2, squared isotropic ratio is [1-(d+1)t^d(t^2+(d+2)(1-t)^2)]/[1-(d+1)t^d]^(1+2/d). It decreases strictly for d>=3, but in d=2 attains minimum 5/6 at t=1/3 and returns to 1 at 1/2. The rectified d=3 endpoint is 2^(-1/3), with sharp d-asymptotic gap.
